objectives.title: Find details in a short text

lessons.explanation: Yo means I, tú informal you, él/ella he/she, and nosotros/nosotras we. Usted uses third-person singular forms; ustedes uses third-person plural forms. Names can be replaced by the matching subject.
examples: Ana y yo → nosotras or nosotros, depending on the group.
commonMistakes: Usted is the listener but takes the él/ella verb form. Yo plus someone else takes nosotros/nosotras.
lessons.provenance: Original Palabra lesson; grammatical rules checked against RAE references. Author review, 2026-10-30; no independent teacher audit.

lessons.explanation: For these regular -ar verbs, keep the stem and add -o, -as, -a, -amos, -áis, -an. The ending identifies who acts. Learn yo → estudio and nosotros → estudiamos; estar is taught separately as irregular.
commonMistakes: Nosotros takes -amos, not -an. Hablo and habló belong to different tenses.
lessons.provenance: Original Palabra lesson; grammatical rules checked against RAE references. Author review, 2026-10-30; no independent teacher audit.

lessons.explanation: An ordinal gives a position: primero, segundo, tercero. Before a masculine singular noun, primero and tercero shorten to primer and tercer. Use a la una but a las dos for at a time.
commonMistakes: Primera agrees with clase. Primer is the shortened form before a masculine singular noun.

stimuli.SpanishText: Los lunes estudio español en la primera clase. La clase es a las ocho. Escucho a la profesora y hablo con mis compañeros. En la segunda clase estudiamos matemáticas. Mi amigo Luis dibuja en la tercera clase, arte. Después, nosotros practicamos deportes. En casa yo uso la computadora y estudio un poco más. Mis amigos escuchan música, pero no trabajan hoy.
stimuli.provenance: Original fictional passage, authored for Palabra. Not a textbook reading.

exercises.feedback: Vosotros/vosotras takes estudiáis. Ustedes takes the third-person plural form instead.

culture.text: Vosotros is used for familiar plural address in much of Spain. Ustedes serves plural address throughout Latin America and in some Spanish regions. Both are valid.
